title: Polar Day / Night Checker: Midnight Sun Test
description: Check whether a place and date fall in polar day or polar night with the Polar Day / Night Checker — midnight sun and winter dark, by latitude. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, Tromsø, Norway (69.65°N) gets a geometric midnight-sun run from about May 23 to July 22 — and a matching polar-night stretch around the December solstice.
quick_answer: The Polar Day / Night Checker tells you whether the Sun rises at all — or sets at all — at a place on a date, from its latitude and the Sun's seasonal declination. Enter place and date and read the verdict: polar day, polar night, or an ordinary day.

Exactly on the Arctic Circle (66.56°N), the Sun just grazes: one day a year it never quite sets, one day it never quite rises — the line is drawn where the grazing happens.

faq: The Sun's centre never dips below the horizon for a full 24 hours — including days when it merely skims. The checker uses the geometric definition and says so.
What about twilight during polar night?
Polar night is not all pitch black: near the circles, midday brings hours of civil twilight — a blue noon without a sunrise.
Why do the circles sit at 66.56°?
90° minus Earth's axial tilt (23.44°). The tilt sets the circles, the tropics, and this checker's thresholds.
Does the checker handle the Antarctic?
Yes — southern latitudes mirror the north with seasons flipped: polar day around December, polar night around June.
Yes — real horizons and atmospheric bending add sunrises at the margins. The checker reports the geometric rule; local almanacs fine-tune.
Can the whole winter really lack sunrise?
At the pole, yes — one sunset in September, one sunrise in March. Settlements like Svalbard's live a ~two-month version of it.
Same phenomenon; 'midnight sun' is the friendlier name. Civil twilight swapping in at the edges is the softer variant the checker also flags by latitude.
Everywhere equatorward of the two circles — which is most of the inhabited world, and why visitors find it so strange.
